description: A multi-arm denylist regex is 'controlled' by negatives that each trip two or more arms; deleting an arm leaves the suite green.
example: atl_v0 geometry_ref: removing the decimal-pair and blank arms left all 3 geometry negatives red-as-expected and the suite green, while 'see 25.1, -80.4' now passed. Fixed: one negative per arm built to evade the others, plus per-arm sabotage (each removal reddens exactly its control).

description: ^…$ under Python re (jsonschema, linkml-validate) accepts 'value\n'; ECMA-262 does not. A YAML | block scalar produces exactly that.
example: atl_v0 sha256 and id patterns accepted '<64 hex>\n' in both declared validators. Fixed: (?!\n)$ on every anchored pattern + neg_sha256_trailing_newline.

recurrences.note: format.checksum '^sha256:…$' (and runspec STREAM_ID/DATE, board SHA) accepted a trailing newline; → \Z with negative cases

description: One control is declared to prove N sibling constraints ('same pattern shape'); the README claims all N while saying 'claimed only where a fixture proves it'.
example: atl_v0: one stream_id control for 5 id slots, one tag control for 7 enums, one evaluation control for closed-ness of all classes. Fixed: a control per sibling (ids, 6 enums, root + part closed-ness) or the claim downgraded to 'generator path, not controlled'.

description: A fixture faithfully copies a source field whose pointer target is wrong; provenance discipline ('nothing from memory') propagates the error instead of catching it.
example: pos_exemplar limitations_ref copied '§12 Where the analogy breaks' from the board entry; the page numbers the section 11. Fixed in both (board entry note → generator fix at M-1d).

recurrences.note: a verbatim prose move carried 'the confident true positive with the longest lead' — a selection rule the code never implemented (it picks the most confident TP with lead >= 2).
F-6/F-7 (M-1d-i): 'a refusal writes nothing' copied into 3 documents while false; 'opens nothing under data/site' survived into contract v0.2.0

description: A perturbation self-test on dense, single-entity synthetic data cannot see defects that only exist with gaps (row-vs-calendar shift, bfill, observed-week horizon) or across entities (reshape order, station→unit mixing).
example: atlantis_core selftest v1 (one unit, 3 samples every week): a back-filled last-known state, a horizon counted in observed weeks, weeks-UNTIL-next-sample and a week-major table scramble all passed; on real data they moved positives 1168→949…1094 or scrambled 15,547 rows. Fixed: 2 patients (one isolable), gaps at t−4/t+2 (primary) and t−1/t (neighbour), daily week t−1, raw frames through normalise; 16 planted defects caught. Fix: Synthesise ≥ 2 entities and deliberate gaps around t; build through the real ingest path; plant each defect class and name the check that catches it.

recurrences.note: F-1 (M-1d-i): gap-dependent label defects invisible on the new daily event-stream shape

rectangle-only zones made a bounding-box mask indistinguishable (F-5), and no gap longer than last_known_weeks made raw vs carried refractory indistinguishable (F-7); → triangle/hole/MultiPolygon zones and an lk+1-week gap after a crossing, each with a plant

description: A window bound tested only from outside (t+H+1 must not move it) lets a shortened window pass. Test both edges: t+H must move it, and t+H alone must keep the outcome known.
example: atlantis_core selftest v1: a label looking H−1 weeks ahead passed C1 (t+1) and C2 (t+H+1); real data positives 1168→949, outcome-unknown drops 1800→2098. Fixed: C2b. Fix: For every window, one control just inside each edge and one just outside.

description: Leak invariance asserted on features and target but not on the ROW FILTERS (already-in-event, unknown-outcome) — the future leaks in through which rows are kept.
example: atlantis_core selftest v1: already_in_event = sig.shift(-1).ffill(4) passed; real data positives 1168→949, prevalence 0.108→0.088. Fixed: C1/C2/C3/C5 assert already_in_event unchanged at every week ≤ t. Fix: Treat every column that decides inclusion as a feature for leakage purposes.

recurrences.note: the trend baseline's leak tests covered s_t but not its sibling input s_prev; planting s_prev = shift(−1) (the step reads s(t+1)) left all 16 baseline tests green while the synthetic trend AUROC went 0.827 → 0.996 → plant S3 + s_prev ≡ the label's carried signal at t − 1 wk on every exemplar unit-week

description: Folding an imputer's missingness-indicator contribution into its vital's SHAP gives data availability (or unit identity) the vital's tag — a structurally-absent stream reads as a lever.
example: atlantis_core logistic swap: discharge_30d_t3 (lever) ranked #3 by mean|φ| 0.702, of which 0.708 came from its missingness flag (units 8/9 have no gauge); the T2 note then misread the top six. Fixed: flags are availability:<vital> pseudo-vitals tagged artifact, net group attribution reported beside abs-sums.

description: A control that cannot fail: additivity of a linear decomposition, refitting the same data, a guard flag set from argument presence, a denylist proven by its own three examples.
example: test_linear_shap_is_exact passed under any column→vital mapping; honoured = fold_tables is not None passed a no-op callable; assert_green passed a dict of 1,640 keyed predictions. Fixed: brute-force interventional φ per column, per-fold rebuild verified, allowlist + size/number caps, the reviewer's three as tests.

recurrences.note: a test named ..._sum_net passed with np.abs sums; board_check compared 5 of ~20 evaluated fields (a doctored Brier passed).
F-3b/F-5 (M-1d-i): tests asserted a one-word status flip ratifies, and an empty #limits section passes

M-1e: a fold check read selected_on, which the same code set from Y; planting fit(s_tr, te) and fold(Y) into the real loop left the suite green. check_thresholds_fixed's positive case used a rule that by signature could not see test. The producer's own first runtime fix recomputed the thresholds it compared against (caught before commit). Fixed: a FitRecorder proxy checks what fit() received; source-level plants P1-P4 into eval must fail by name.

the board's embargo guard walked headline, swaps and folds but not the ablation variants or the sensitivity run whose numbers it publishes under 'every boundary'; unembargoing either passed 76 tests and emitted → assert_embargo walks every variant and the sensitivity block; real-path plants Q2/Q3

assert_comparators was documented as arithmetic on the RESULT but holds by construction for the real eval (rate and positives/n from one frame); its plants were all result-dict mutations → documented as a tamper check; slot ↔ result equality added; the eval-time checks B1/B2 and plants S1–S3 are the controls

description: A 'training-relevant' hash omits fields that choose which models are trained or which numbers the keyed record carries, and is stamped onto results it does not describe.
example: semantic_hash was unchanged under eval.ablations / sensitivity_threshold / vital group; the logistic swap file carried the xgboost-learner hash; lever_stations (what-if only) moved it. Fixed, each case a test.

recurrences.note: generalised to a cache key: the CRW per-zone cache omitted grid pin, pad and variable; → keyed by all three

the M-2a-i cache-key fix keyed three of the four basis fields and dropped base: a new base after a deleted artifact read the old source's spans (0 requests) under the new base's stamp; the generic ERDDAP cache keyed none → CRW key + base/zlev tag, ERDDAP basis subdir (base, variable, zlev, box); a plant without the base reproduces it

description: A control asserts the data a visual element needs, never that the element is drawn; the page's words then describe a mark that is not there.
example: Strips asserted split=None for excluded weeks; the template drew them as zero-width rects (x0 == x1 on a date axis), invisible since v0. Fixed: bands computed in Python as week-wide intervals and tested; checked rendered in a browser.

recurrences.note: conform item 10's new path read the page's embedded copy and passed a page whose script throws and draws nothing — the very defect the producer had just fixed (a // comment in a one-line IIFE killed every chart while 676 tests passed; found only in a browser) → item 10 needs the section renderer and a script that passes node --check (steward ruling 25); node --check test on the template

description: A build-time validator (Python) accepts what the runtime renderer (JS) cannot read: negative list indices, tokens in fields the renderer inserts verbatim, unknown format names, a figure id placed twice.
example: resolve('a.-1') passed; {{…}} in a section nav/strip label rendered literally; |pct rendered a raw float; a duplicated {{fig:pr}} gave duplicate DOM ids. Fixed: one grammar enforced on both sides, each case a planted test.

recurrences.note: the board validator (closed AtlEvaluation) did not constrain what the markdown renderer emits: newlines/'|' in limitations_ref and superseded_by wrote a heading onto BOARD.md; → closed top level, refuse control chars, escape '|'

description: A checker's hard-coded minimum is a strict subset of the template it guards, and its globs run on unnormalised paths, so the template's own protections can be deleted or walked around silently.
example: mapping --check passed with **/*.csv, site/**, geojson removed and with './data/…' as a source; edge_properties and json_properties were never checked; stamps were checked for presence, not value. Fixed: minimum = the template's fence, posixpath-normalised matching, edge/json/stamp-value checks, 11 more planted defects.

recurrences.note: F-3/F-5 (M-1d-i): posture check weaker than the ADR template's 4-field block; items 1/2/10/12 weaker than their rows

description: A check is extended to a new input shape, but the synthetic features that expose defects (gaps, edge cases) stay tied to the old shape, and the old shape's planted-defect suite is not re-run on the new one.
example: selftest let the event stream be daily (M-1d-i); the t+2 / neighbour-at-t gaps stayed point-only. in_event_bfill (a future leak into the row filter) and label_rowshift passed on both forked hypoxia instances while the exemplar caught them. Fixed: the event stream carries those gaps whatever its shape, and the whole 12-defect catalogue runs against two forked worlds.

description: To fix a vacuity failure, a fallback moves the probe somewhere it cannot detect the defect it exists for. A loud refusal becomes a silent pass, and nothing reports the check that was lost.
example: gap_week moved the gap 'one past the span' when it hit a vital's lag; with lags {0,1,2} or {0,1} no gap lay between t−L and t, and a lag counted in rows passed. Fixed: C8 calendar-lag invariance (deleting (t−L, t] must not move a lag-L vital), and the run reports when C8 alone guards a stream.

recurrences.note: with the peer validator absent (every public clone) the lattice check exited 0 and its _graph silently dropped dangling edges; → local re-checks edge refs + duplicate ids, NOT RUN is printed

the C9 boundary probe was skipped on a condition broader than the carry it guarded (R+1 passed the whole self-test at R=4, iid), and the episode check returned 'not checked' without a word; → the gap week is filled and the probe always runs, an unrecomputable signal is refused, and C9's outcome is on the receipt

description: A check described as 'resolves inside X' is implemented as (root / p).is_file(). An absolute or ../ path satisfies it, so a gate can be met by a file outside X.
example: The fetch posture gate opened on Atlantis's own ratified ADR-000; conform item 7 passed on a sibling instance's ADR; fork wrote an absolute scratchpad path into units.yaml. Fixed: resolve() + is_relative_to(root), with ../ and absolute paths planted as tests.

description: A human-approval gate reads a one-word field an agent can edit (frontmatter status), while the document's real ratification is a signed block the gate never parses.
example: posture ADR: the dry run 'ratified' it by flipping status: proposed → ratified with the 4-field table still blank; the fetch CLI and conform item 7 (fetched) both passed. Fixed: parse the Ratification row (decision, ratified-by, ISO date, ratified) and require the frontmatter to agree.

description: A 'writes only its own X' gate tests a path that another flag can point anywhere, not the identity it protects.
example: board --entries: the outside-instance refusal checked that --outputs sat inside the entries' repo; --outputs pointed at the exemplar wrote Atlantis's board pairing one instance's config with another's metrics. Fixed: gate on the instance root, and require --outputs inside it.

recurrences.note: the board compared each boundary's window end against the record's own next_start, never the split; a boundary relabelled to guard 2021 emitted → expected years derived from inst.cfg.split

description: A hash/pin check runs only if the target exists, so a deleted or mistyped target turns the check into a silent pass.
example: datasets --check: deleting a grandfathered parquet or typo-ing its path left all three records ✅. Fixed: absent bytes the record promises are an error; otherwise a printed 'pin not verified' note.

description: 'A precedes B (a gate)' implemented as 'a path A→B exists' passes when a bypass edge is added; a gate needs dominance.
example: lattice: an added declarations→fetch edge skipped selftest and all three checks passed. Fixed: every source→fetch path must pass selftest (dominance), with the bypass edge planted.

description: A safety refusal fed by subprocess git output treats an error (no repo, wrong branch) as 'no evidence' and permits the act.
example: board --regenerate: origin/main hard-coded; in an instance repo on master the pushed entry was overwritten. Fixed: check return codes, read every remote-tracking ref, refuse when there is no repo/remote/upstream.

recurrences.note: run_controls.sh read grep exit 2 (a bad or option-like pattern) as 'all named': a REJECTS_ON starting with '-' left linkml-validate's reason test vacuous since 0.5.0, and the -e fix cured one cause only → rc read whole, 2 = instrument failure

description: A temporal-split check tests each row's timestamp, but the label reads t+1..t+H, so the last H steps of a fit or stop set are labelled by the held-out period.
example: M-1e check_fold_selection: stop year 2022 had 10 of 31 positives labelled by 2023 (test) onsets; the check passed by row year. Disclosed by operator ruling; embargo carded (idea_label_horizon_embargo).

description: A provenance field (threshold_from, selected_on) is written from the config's intent rather than from what the code did, and the gate reads only the field, so any defect beneath it emits clean.
example: M-1e lead_time threshold_from stamped from eval.threshold_from; a test-quantile lead threshold reproduced v1's 0.6818 under 'val' and board emit accepted it. Fixed: the lead time records alert_threshold; eval and the board check its identity with the fixed budget threshold, and realised = n_alerts / n_test by arithmetic.

recurrences.note: the CRW reduction block omitted the zone file / pad it was computed over, so a cache-first fetch after a re-pin emitted the old zones cleanly; → the basis (grid_sha256 · pad_deg · variable · base) is recorded and a different basis is refused by fetch, --verify and conform item 3

embargo_weeks documented as written 'from the boundaries it CHECKED' was the config-resolved E; a plant claiming 6 wk over 4-wk cuts emitted → reworded; the board requires rows_dropped ≥ the H-window crossing count
the summary's reduction.base came from the spec while the bytes came from a cache keyed without it, so the basis check passed on the old source's bytes

the board entry's config_bytes_md5 was stamped at run time and the config's board block was edited before the commit, so the entry named bytes no commit holds (the semantic hash did not move) → the board refuses an entry whose recorded bytes are not the file's; the entry re-issued as v2 (rulings 24, 26)

description: A per-entity loop keys caches, rows and records by an id the input format does not guarantee unique; duplicates collide silently.
example: CRW fetch keyed its cache and reduction by the zone id; a zone exported as two features with seg=5 hit the first feature's cache (wrong envelope, a fallback 1° away), wrote duplicate (seg, date) rows and overwrote the first record. Fixed: PolygonGrid, conform item 1 and fork refuse duplicate ids.

description: Documentation states that config X makes module A agree with module B, no test pairs the two modules, and the claim is wrong — while the next mission is about to set X on its strength.
example: 'R = H makes the label's onset the one eval/lead.py counts' (docstring, schema slot, README, skill, test world): it is R = H − 1; R = H drops the only positive row of an onset H+1 weeks after the previous crossing. Fixed: doctrine corrected (operator ruling), tests/test_label_refractory.py pairs label.make with lead_time (coverage 1.0 at H−1, 0.5 at H).

description: A temporal boundary stated in calendar years is enforced in the binning's year (ISO-Monday weeks): the year's last bin holds days of the next calendar year, so the check is exact in bins while prose claims calendar years.
example: M-1f embargo: exact in week-years; under a calendar-date perturbation 1 kept training and 5 kept validation labels read 1–5 January (the 2019-12-30 week). Fixed: README 2b states the convention; a raw-stream perturbation test binned as the label is.

description: A leakage check re-derives the label window from the same helper the cut uses, and no test perturbs the labeller's own input — a shared off-by-one would pass both cut and check.
example: M-1f: embargo() and check_label_windows() both use _window_end; only hand-pinned counts guarded them. Fixed: tests/test_embargo_perturbation.py inflates raw event observations past each boundary, rebuilds through label.make — 0 kept labels move, every dropped one does, a cut one week short leaks. Related C-006, C-025.

description: A wait loop or gate tests a cheap proxy for availability (an index page answering 200) instead of the real operation at its real size, so it waits on a condition that can never make the operation succeed.
example: M-2a-ii: a probe-gated fetch loop ran 39 attempts over ~2¼ h on index.html=200 while CRW's proxy cut every request at ~10.3 s and a 5-year chunk took ~40 s — futile by construction. Found by timing requests against chunk size (2 d 0.5 s → 1 yr >10 s); fixed by 15-day union spans (core 0.5.2). Related C-023.

description: A completeness claim is made by counting nulls in the rows that arrived, which cannot see rows that never arrived.
example: M-2a-ii: FKNMS DHW 'no nulls' over 1985-03-25→2025-12-31 read as complete; 1999-05-01 is absent for all 21 zones (CRW's own axis). Fixed: provenance.daily_completeness (distinct days vs calendar span, dates_per_unit) in ERDDAP/CRW summaries; fetch --verify prints ⓘ; the instance discloses the gap (steward ruling 17).

description: A descriptive drift is recorded with an untested cause stated as fact, where confounders in the data's own provenance are known and unexcluded.
example: M-2a-ii: 'the train→test base-rate rise is warming itself' (instance STATE, AAR) while CoralTemp's 2002 input change (the OSTIA residual its posture ADR discloses) and DHW's fixed MMM climatology were not separated. Fixed: 'consistent with warming; not separated from …'. SO-4/SO-9 neighbour.

description: A threshold-free precision metric (AUPRC) is compared across labels or row sets with different prevalence and read as inflation or improvement, with no lift, base-rate normalisation, or a comparator measured on the same rows.
example: M-2b T3: persistence-inclusive label AUPRC 0.929 vs onset 0.690 read as 'inflation' — prevalence 0.270 vs 0.150 and 7,644 vs 5,595 test rows; the model's lift fell 4.60 → 3.44. The honest signal: the no-model persistence comparator closing on the model (52% → 88% of its AUPRC). Fixed: lift reported; falsifier restated so prevalence cannot meet it.

description: A status roll-up line (register summary, AAR headline, STATE) claims more support than the rows it summarises say.
example: M-2b: the thesis register's 'Reading' line listed T3 and T10 as supported-by-two-instances while T3's row said the exemplar run was not repeated and T10's row said one instance-sourced entry. Fixed: 'tested on one instance (FKNMS)'.
